examples: The standardised Chebyshev bound needs positive variance; zero variance gives a counterexample at k=2.
For a general random variable, P(X>t) and P(X>=t) differ at atoms; survival explanations should keep the strict inequality.
Finite support is also countable, so an MCQ must distinguish a general criterion from a sufficient special case.
